# Mainframe entity refinements

Entity refinements specialize upstream OpenTelemetry entities with additional
identity and description attributes specific to the
Mainframe domain.

| Refinement ID | Refined Entity Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `refinement.mainframe.host` | `host` | Mainframe refinement of the generic host entity for the IBM Z Central Processing Complex (CPC). A CPC is a physical bare-metal server — the mainframe equivalent of any host. The IBM Z-specific attributes (serial number, machine type, machine model) extend the generic host description while preserving full compatibility with consumers that understand the base host entity. |


## `refinement.mainframe.host`

Refines upstream entity: `host`

**Status:** ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)

Mainframe refinement of the generic host entity for the IBM Z Central Processing Complex (CPC). A CPC is a physical bare-metal server — the mainframe equivalent of any host. The IBM Z-specific attributes (serial number, machine type, machine model) extend the generic host description while preserving full compatibility with consumers that understand the base host entity.

**Type:** `host`

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[1] `host.id`:** `<machine type>-<serial number>` of the Central Processing Complex (CPC), with leading zeros removed from the serial, e.g. `3931-45A01`; equal to `virtualization.platform.id`. The HMC Web Services API (CPC `machine-type`, `cpc-serial-number`), z/OS RMF (SMF type 70) and Linux on IBM Z (`/proc/sysinfo`) all report it.

**[2] `host.arch`:** SHOULD be set to "s390x" for IBM Z and LinuxONE systems.

**[3] `host.name`:** The name of the Central Processing Complex (CPC) as configured on the HMC (CPC object field `name`). Descriptive only: a CPC can be renamed without becoming a different CPC.

**[4] `host.type`:** SHOULD be the concatenation of the IBM machine type and model of the Central Processing Complex (CPC), e.g., "9175-ME1".

**[5] `mainframe.host.machine_model`:** IBM machine model tier (e.g. "ME1"). Combined with mainframe.host.machine_type this forms the full type-model string that populates host.type.

**[6] `mainframe.host.machine_type`:** IBM four-digit machine type (e.g. "9175"). Consumers that understand only the base host entity should use host.type instead.

**[7] `mainframe.host.serial_number`:** Mainframe-specific serial number of the CPC; also part of host.id.

**[8] `host.ip`:** IPv4 Addresses MUST be specified in dotted-quad notation. IPv6 addresses MUST be specified in the [RFC 5952](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5952.html) format.

**[9] `host.mac`:** MAC Addresses MUST be represented in [IEEE RA hexadecimal form](https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/import/documents/tutorials/eui.pdf): as hyphen-separated octets in uppercase hexadecimal form from most to least significant.

---

`host.arch` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.
